title: Python SDK: streaming chat fanout API + sideband event ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams using the Python SDK want a clear, low-friction way to consume streaming chat completions while simultaneously receiving non-content sideband events (e.g., rate limit warnings, model switch hints, token-level metadata). Existing iterator and callback patterns either conflate content and sideband events or force awkward ad-hoc parsing in product code.

Goal: Design and implement a Python SDK surface that lets callers: (1) receive token/content events incrementally, (2) subscribe to sideband events via a stable typed surface, (3) fan out the stream to multiple consumer patterns (sync iterator, async iterator, callback, queue), and (4) expose resumable checkpoint tokens + idempotent-apply semantics for retries. The API should emphasize ergonomic defaults (bounded backpressure, automatic checkpointing on successful application) and be compatible with sync and async codebases.

Scope: prototype API surface, core runtime plumbing for fanout + sideband parsing, tests for retry resume path, examples for sync/async usage, docs and migration notes. Not in scope: new server-side protocol changes — implement client-side compatibility with current streaming wire format (delta events + JSON sideband frames).
acceptance_criteria: Public API: provide `ChatStream` object with methods: `subscribe_sideband(handler)`, `as_async_iter()`, `as_sync_iter()`, `subscribe_callback(cb, *, max_buffer=128)`, and `checkpoint()` returning a resumable token string.
Sideband events delivered as typed enums: RATE_LIMIT, MODEL_HINT, USAGE_STATS, SOURCE_CHANGE with structured payloads; handlers receive (event_type, payload, timestamp).
Backpressure: default bounded queue per subscriber with configurable `max_buffer` and clear documentation of blocking vs dropping strategy. Tests for both behaviors.

Retry/resume: Demonstrate end-to-end resume using checkpoint token with idempotent-apply example in README + unit tests that simulate transient connection errors and replays without duplication when handler marks frames applied.
Documentation: migration guide + 3 runnable examples (sync iterator, async iterator with `async for`, and callback-based fanout).
Benchmarks: microbenchmark showing added latency vs existing iterator-only approach (target < 3ms median overhead for moderate token rates).

implementation_steps: API design PR: finalize function signatures + typed enums (1d)
Runtime: implement fanout dispatcher and per-subscriber bounded queues with configurable policies (2d)
Checkpointing: design token format (opaque string) and idempotent-apply helper contract (1d)
Sideband parsing: stable parser that maps wire frames to enums + payload validation (1d)
Examples & docs: three usage patterns + migration guide (1d)
Tests: unit tests for resume/retry scenarios, backpressure behavior, and sideband delivery ordering (2d)
Benchmarks & perf: microbench against iterator baseline and tune (1d)
Release notes + changelog entry for python-sdk-0.8.0
risks: Server frames may evolve; we need a fallback path for unknown sideband types to avoid breaking user handlers.
Fanout adds memory overhead per-subscriber — risk for customers with many subscribers; mitigated by default bounded queues and guidance in docs.
Checkpoint token format must remain opaque; exposing internals risks coupling and future incompatibility.
Complexity of dual sync/async API surfaces — ensure a single core implementation to avoid drift and duplicated bugs.
test_plan: Unit: parser unit tests mapping wire frames -> enums and payload validation.
Unit: fanout dispatcher tests for correct delivery ordering across subscribers.
Integration: simulate connection drop and replay using checkpoint token; verify idempotent apply prevents duplicates.
Load: create 50 concurrent subscribers with bounded queues and measure memory and latency impact.
Docs: run examples in CI smoke test for both sync and async examples.
notes:
API example (sync iterator):
from redwood import ChatStream
stream = client.chat_stream(... )
for frame in stream.as_sync_iter():
    if frame.type == 'content':
        print(frame.text)
    elif frame.type == 'sideband':
        handle_sideband(frame.sideband_type, frame.payload)

API example (async):
async for frame in stream.as_async_iter():
    # same handling as above

Callback subscription example:
def on_sideband(event_type, payload, ts):
    # quick non-blocking handler
    metrics.increment('sideband.' + event_type)

stream.subscribe_sideband(on_sideband)

Idempotent-apply pattern: handlers call `stream.mark_applied(offset_token)` when they have durably processed a logical frame. On resume the SDK will replay from the earliest unapplied offset. This keeps server-side semantics simple and gives users control over dedupe boundaries.
We will iterate on naming if feedback from Python SDK users indicates discoverability problems.
